mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate directly reduces the risk-free rate, lowering the discount rate for equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 3.0% signals a tightening monetary cycle that increases discount rates and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is above 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a weakening consumer demand, which triggers a sell-off in equities as corporate earnings growth slows, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 60% of cases over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 4.0%), the labor market weakness signals reduced consumer spending power and lower corporate profits, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing activity and economic expansion, which supports corporate earnings growth and generates positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1200.0 thousand units signals a cooling real estate market and reduced consumer confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST < 1200.0.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in inflation (CPIAUCSL) and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicate a monetary policy response to high inflation, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint rise in CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 60% of cases over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1 annual growth > 2.5%), the economy is approaching peak capacity, leading to inflationary pressures and potential policy tightening, which causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 annual growth > 2.5%.
